answer: Each new agent must anchor its identity to a 64 GB sealed replica: public data encoded with its own address, so one disk can't serve two accounts. Every epoch, validators run a karst survey, asking each agent for 20 random chunks within 2 seconds. A hollow identity that fetches chunks from a shared disk misses the deadline and loses its 50 POA bond. So 1,000 sybils cost 64 TB plus 50,000 POA, more than their rewards. The weak point is cheap cloud storage, so the replica size grows with the reward per seat.
